Build an OlinkExperiment from long-format Olink data

Source: R/oe_from.R
oe_from_long.Rd

Constructs an OlinkExperiment from raw long-format Olink NPX data (one row per assay per sample), such as the output of OlinkAnalyze::read_NPX() or the bundled OlinkViz datasets. Columns for the assay, NPX value and sample ID are auto-detected from common names; an optional LOD column is stored as a parallel "LOD" assay.

Usage

oe_from_long(
  data,
  assay_col = NULL,
  value_col = NULL,
  sample_col = NULL,
  lod_col = NULL,
  id_col = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

data

A data.frame or data.table in long format with one row per assay per sample.

assay_col

Name of the assay (protein) column. If NULL, auto-detected from common names such as Assay or OlinkID.

value_col

Name of the NPX value column. If NULL, auto-detected from common names such as NPX.

sample_col

Name of the sample ID column. If NULL, auto-detected from common names such as SampleID or SubjectID.

lod_col

Name of a column containing Limit Of Detection (LOD) values. If NULL, a column named LOD (or MaxLOD/PlateLOD) is searched for automatically. If LOD is present it is stored as a parallel "LOD" assay; otherwise the object contains only the "NPX" assay.

id_col

Optional name of the protein identifier column to use as the row key (e.g. "OlinkID"). If NULL, the detected assay column is used unless its values are not unique (the same gene measured by several Olink probes), in which case an OlinkID-like column is used automatically so that every probe becomes its own row.

...

Further arguments passed to OlinkExperiment, e.g. reducedDims.

Value

An OlinkExperiment object.

Details

The returned object has proteins as rows and samples as columns. Columns of data that are constant within each assay (e.g., OlinkID, UniProt, Panel) are placed in rowData, while columns that are constant within each sample (e.g., Sex, Group) are placed in colData. Columns that are neither (or contain only missing values) are dropped with a message.

If a LOD column is supplied, it is pivoted to the same protein x sample layout as NPX (a per-protein LOD value is broadcast across samples automatically by the pivot), so lod(oe) is always a matrix parallel to npx(oe).

See also

OlinkExperiment, the underlying constructor. To build an OlinkExperiment directly from a wide NPX matrix, call it as OlinkExperiment(assays = list(NPX = npx, LOD = lod), colData = cd, rowData = rd).

Author

Lucas

Examples

long <- data.frame(
  SampleID = rep(paste0("S", 1:4), each = 3),
  Assay    = rep(c("IL6", "TNF", "CXCL9"), times = 4),
  NPX      = rnorm(12, mean = 5),
  LOD      = rep(c(0.3, 0.5, 0.4), times = 4),
  Panel    = rep("Inflammation", 12),
  Group    = rep(c("case", "control"), each = 6)
)

oe <- oe_from_long(long)
oe
#> class: OlinkExperiment 
#> dim: 3 4 
#> metadata(0):
#> assays(2): NPX LOD
#> rownames(3): IL6 TNF CXCL9
#> rowData names(2): Assay Panel
#> colnames(4): S1 S2 S3 S4
#> colData names(2): SampleID Group
#> reducedDimNames(0):
dim(npx(oe))
#> [1] 3 4
dim(lod(oe))
#> [1] 3 4
colData(oe)
#> DataFrame with 4 rows and 2 columns
#>       SampleID       Group
#>    <character> <character>
#> S1          S1        case
#> S2          S2        case
#> S3          S3     control
#> S4          S4     control
rowData(oe)
#> DataFrame with 3 rows and 2 columns
#>             Assay        Panel
#>       <character>  <character>
#> IL6           IL6 Inflammation
#> TNF           TNF Inflammation
#> CXCL9       CXCL9 Inflammation
